text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Economic researchers expect Austria's economy to grow again. Projections of 0.7 percent growth might be revised upward, as Germany's economy is gaining strength as well. But Austria's current account deficit is growing.

- Technical engineering firm Simmering-Graz-Pauker, a branch of Siemens, has received an order worth 1.1 billion schillings to produce train carriages for Croatia's national railways. Production is now secured for the next five years, Siemens Oesterreich chief Alfred Hochleitner said.
- Austria's largest bakery company Ankerbrot is to cooperate with Upper Austrian baker Fischer, enabling bakery services across werstern Austria.
- Austrian trade regulations are to be renewed from July 1, 1997. The new regulations will streamline bureaucratic procedures.
- Petrol price in Austria rose and oil and chemicals company OMV said the main reason was higher crude prices in Rotterdam following the U.S. missile attacks on Iraq.
- German tyre-maker Continental does not expect former Austrian finance minister Hannes Androsch to take over its Austrian unit Semperit.

- Austrian insurance companies might have the last word in the sale of the government's stake in Creditanstalt bank. Bundeslaender Versicherung might take over Germany's Commerzbank's stake in the consortium to buy Creditanstalt.
- Austrians are consuming as much as ever, study by economic research institute Wifo says. People are trying to keep up their living standards by taking money out of their savings accounts.
- Austrian sparkline wine producer Schlumberger reported operating profits were up to 17.5 million schillings after a loss of 4.7 million the previous year.
- Luxury hosiery maker plans a full listing at the New York Stock Exchange by 1997.
